steps.content:
March 15, N.F. 113, 19:48
Senior Management Hidden Office, Drifter Camp

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Wow... Is this your headquarters? It's old and shabby, but feels very Syndican. It actually looks pretty cool.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: What's this? A model of the Drifter Camp? These look like buttons you can press.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: This is a personal office. The model is the general operation panel for the Drifter Camp's major mechanisms.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Don't touch it. Save us some trouble.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hmph... So, architect... Did you build this whole Drifter Camp, including those mechanisms, secret passages, and that weird building?
He doesn't answer and turns to face you, with a weary expression and steady voice, but he speaks with indisputable certainty.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: I'd like to have a few words with Minos' Chief. If everyone else could give us some privacy.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I won't leave Chief.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: You can summon your guard and let it stay here to protect ${PlayerName}. I can't see it, and I don't mind being watched.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hmph, your guys seem to mind though.
Someone tries to say something, but Julien lifts a hand to quiet him.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: My guys will leave too. Only I'll stay. You can take me as your hostage.

He pulls out a gun with the barrel pointed at himself as he speaks, and hands the gun to you. The bony, gloomy face now has a tight frown on it. His eyes are deep-set, and there is neither hint of a smile nor vitality in his expression.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Look at me. What threat can a body like this pose? You came to stop Mania, didn't you? Then time is not on your side.
Grr...
Amid the tense atmosphere, someone's stomach suddenly growls.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...What? Don't look at me like that! It wasn't me! I already had enough buns! I...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Hecate, you haven't eaten anything, have you? Since this morning?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: That's not important. It's Nightmare who fought in the battles. I didn't use too much energy.
Grr... Hecate's face is blank, but Nightmare, who's next to her, flinches.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: ...Sigh.
The man's face loosens up. He sighs almost inaudibly and puts the gun on the desk. Turning the wheelchair, he makes his way to another corner swiftly and skillfully, then presses the button there.
A sketchy mechanical arm extends from the bookshelves, taking something from the top drawer and bringing it before Hella.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Oh ****, what are you doing?
The arm loosens. Something drops. She catches it reflexively, looking like the thing scalds her hand, only to find it's a pack of... candies in some old-fashioned packaging.
Julien moves near a desktop receiver and leans in to whisper something into it.
Soon, a red-haired woman pushes open the door and comes in. She comprehends the situation almost instantly and flashes a knowing smile at Julien.

steps.speaker: Red-haired Woman
steps.content: Hehe, you've improved, Boss. You didn't pull a long face till the end and knew to send for me to serve our guests.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: ...Just some starving kids. Get them out of here quickly.

steps.speaker: Red-haired Woman
steps.content: Alright, alright. You've seen it yourselves, he's a boring man. Don't waste time on him. Follow me, kiddos.

steps.speaker: Red-haired Woman
steps.content: There are some late-night snacks ready in the canteen. We've sent away those caped kids so they won't make a mess here.

steps.speaker: Red-haired Woman
steps.content: Don't worry about your friend. That boy may look like a twig, but I bet he can take out ten Juliens without breaking a sweat. Perhaps you can grab something for him too?
steps.female_content: Don't worry about your friend. That girl may look like a twig, but I bet she can take out ten Juliens without breaking a sweat. Perhaps you can grab something for her too?

steps.speaker: Red-haired Woman
steps.content: You guys have some big fights waiting for you ahead. If you don't fuel up, how can you protect your loved ones?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: No, I...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If they're going to kill me, it won't happen here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Eat well. Don't starve yourself again.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Okay, if this is your wish.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: But Nightmare will stay. No one can hurt you.
The two Sinners are pushed out of the office and the footsteps fade out. The door shuts, leaving only you, Julien, Nightmare who's invisible to him, and icy silence in the room.
Just now, his subordinate's jokes didn't anger or ease him. He watches you like he's waiting for something. You suddenly remember there is still an unoccupied gun between you two.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I understand your eager intention to team up, but I have no interest in taking hostages.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I don't need such a thing. I have my own power, and I'm not interested in taking you hostage.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I need an explanation for everything that's happened so far. This conversation could have happened sooner, and in a friendlier manner.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: I hoped so too. But as you can see, I can't neglect the fact that you were with the Executive Committee. I must verify your stance.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: You've seen how far they can go to eradicate the Drifter Camp. I'm sorry to have dragged you into this conflict, but you gotta do what you gotta do.

steps.speaker: Options (Repeated Choice)
options: Why would the Executive Committee want to do that?
Including shooting that executive officer named Donald?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is an official operation. It must have a convincing motive.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Did Burns have any motives when he dealt with the Legion? I thought all they needed was a decision.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: <size=32>One and a half months ago, when BR-004 precipitated Hypercubes for the first time, the Executive Committee decided to wipe out the Drifter Camp. Be it Mania or a riot, they'll either fabricate a crime for us or force us to commit it. The result will be the same.</size>

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: I've got a question for those big shots. Why have they chosen to pick on a bunch of refugees who's already lost everything, but not those lawless thugs out there?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I only wanted to take apart that weapon and settle the conflict, but you cut off all negotiations and didn't hesitate for a second when you killed him.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why? Because a corpse can't talk? Or did you spoil my stance on purpose to force me to go against the Executive Committee?

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Bad blood. He was just a traitor.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Ask anyone in the camp for his back story. You may not believe it if I tell you, and I don't want to talk about it either.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: And don't worry about your stance. Even in the committee, he was just a disposable pawn. A lapdog who resorted to betraying his home would never be significant.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: When it's over, someone will forge a report to help you get away with this.

steps.speaker: Options
options: It sounds like you have spies in the Executive Committee too?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You know about their internal decision one and a half months ago, and you can forge the executive officer's death investigation report.
His silence confirms your guess.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No wonder the moment I arrived at Keylan Square, you were already after me.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Yes. Information about you is too ambiguous and unreliable, but you've indeed influenced Syndicate greatly. Your existence is too important. We must approach you ourselves and find out whose side you're on.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then why did you assign such an important mission to a mindless kid?

steps.speaker: Taran
steps.content: Shoot me!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: He didn't try to kill me, but took my companions hostage and forced me to shoot him. Instead of testing my friendliness, he wanted me to start a fire. He wanted war.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: As a leader, is this your usual way of dealing with issues? Is this how you manage your underlings?

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: You're right. He's naive and only wants to vent. He's far from an ideal candidate for the job. It was my mistake to have picked him.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: But those who are mature and reliable enough to deal with things have already died doing that in many different ways. All we have left are a bunch of angry kids and an architect who's been chosen to be a makeshift leader.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: It requires considerable capability to deal with things, but our opponent doesn't think we're qualified.
The man's mask-like stiff face finally displays emotions for the first time: frustration, exhaustion, sadness... and a stubborn insistence.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: People didn't gather here to fight. They only wanted a shelter, probably their last one.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: When the Drifter Camp is threatened, some pick up their weapons in rage, but more have already lost the will to fight in the hardships they've been through. They could easily fall into panic.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: We're not the Legion. We don't have their strong fighters, let alone a leader like Zoya who can command a battle.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: I wouldn't have brought conflicts into the Drifter Camp if I'd had a choice. I just never expected that Mania would creep in too.
He pauses as if to collect himself, and stares right at you as he speaks.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: That's the only explanation I can give. You can send someone to confirm the results of the negotiations initiated by the Executive Committee three weeks ago. I can supply communication tools.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: But don't alert the committee, and don't let anyone in the camp know. I don't want any panic.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: You've helped us through the crisis and proven your distinct character. Now, back to the initial reason why I brought you here.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Please go inside the Drifter Camp, investigate the Mania contamination, and rid us of its threat. I'm willing to provide any information and assistance on this. I believe this is also what you need.
He turns to adjust the communication device, then moves to make way for you.

steps.speaker: Options
options: When I leave here, I'll find time to contact the support staff

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's begin. This conversation happened too late, we must seize the time.

steps.speaker: Options
options: It seems that you've had an understanding of Mania in the camp since early on.

steps.content: He nods.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: The earliest suspicion came from the undercover executive officers who infiltrated the Drifter Camp. At first, their main purpose was to spy for intel and scout the landscape. They were obviously preparing for a raid.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: In response, we tightened up our entry control, and monitored and misled those spying executive officers.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: But there was an anomaly ten days ago. The undercover officers suddenly mutated with Mania. Luckily, the person monitoring the officer reacted quickly, prevented a large-scale panic and the spreading of contamination.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: <size=32>Rustfire members didn't reveal this to the inhabitants, but it caused quite a stir within the group. Many thought it was a vicious plot by the Executive Committee, that they had crossed the line and resorted to using Mania like those thugs did in the past.</size>
That's why they were extra sensitive to you, a Mania expert accompanied by executive officers.

steps.speaker: Options
options: ...It would have been simpler had that been all.

steps.content: The highly elusive corruption symptoms, the weird happenings at the Ring ruins in the square, the bizarre marks, the spreading evil contamination field, and Parma which you're investigating. You tell all of these to Julien.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: ...We don't know much about the invisible Mania you mentioned. And the power that triggers Black Rings... Have they really come here?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What's wrong?

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Nothing... I just don't want that tragedy to repeat itself.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: I kept the scene where the executive officers mutated. The remaining contamination is hard to remove, but that also helped to preserve the scene. You can start your investigation from there. I'll send some people to assist you.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Given my condition, I'll be wasting everyone's time if I'm there. I'll stay here to operate the mechanisms and back you up.
You nod and leave with the communications device, but stop and turn around after a second thought.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I have one more question.

steps.speaker: Options
options: Is Dudu one of your guys too?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did she tell you about my suspended animation, or did you discover that first and send her to monitor me?

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: She's not one of us, only an occasional partner. Dudu goes to Romanesque often and is sensitive to death. She just happened to have discovered you.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: That Sinner loves the Drifter Camp, and naturally she cares about your stance. Her conclusion matters greatly to me.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aren't you going to stay with me?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: No need. I believe you now.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: It's a life on thin ice here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If I fail any of your trials, what will you do?

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: If you ever choose to harm the Drifter Camp, I'll do anything I can to end you.
He's so placidly honest.

steps.speaker: Options
options: And now? Have I passed all my trials?

steps.content: This time, Julien doesn't answer. With his face in the shade, you can't see his expression clearly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Haha, excuse me. I said one question. You've been generous enough already, thank you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've sent back the primary investigation report. The FAC has recalled military support to the Executive Committee at the last minute. Until I finish my investigation on Mania, there won't be any threat against you with that level of weaponry.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I can't make any promises further than that. Our mutual trust stops there, and I don't have that kind of power to help you fight against anything.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: That will suffice. You don't need to trust or recognize me, and it doesn't matter if you choose not to forgive us.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: No matter which side you're on, if you're an honorable and kind person, you'll do what you should. Rustfire will never harm you.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: I wish you all the best.
You push open the door to leave. Two people stand behind the door on the left and right. Hecate and Taran. They seem to have guarded the door for a long time and the air between them is stiff.
The moment he sees you, Taran turns his head to look away. You ignore him too and say to Hecate...

steps.speaker: Options
options: Why didn't you go and eat something?

steps.content: Before she answers, the metal beneath your feet begins thumping. Someone is dashing this way from the other end of the bridge.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I'm back! Here, open your mouths!
Hella hops and bumps into both of you, ready to shove the wraps in her hands into your mouths.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hehehe, these are offerings to the marvelous Hella. I'm kind enough to share them with you!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: The way I defeated that huge armor and saved the Drifter Camp was too darn cool, the guys at the canteen were practically kneeling to me. I had my mouth full without paying a dime there.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Ah! I'd never enjoyed this kind of privilege before. I ******* love this place!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Offerings are for the dead.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Mmph... Shut your big mouth!
You take the wrap and pass it to Hecate, then pat the grumpy Hella on her head.
You lead the two of them out of this stressful space that seems to suffocate you.
